title: Sieve for 'poor' failures: #{C ≤ X : ω(4Cp+1) ≤ 5} ≪ X (log log X)⁵/log X — pointwise in p by an upper-bound sieve (Hardy–Ramanujan / Brun) — so most C have rich 4Cp+1
connection: Upper-bound sieves bound the number of C ≤ X for which the linear form 4Cp+1 has few prime factors (almost-prime values of a linear polynomial): ≪ X/log X · (log log X)^k uniformly in p ≤ X^A? (Need uniformity in the coefficient 4p: standard sieve bounds for almost-primes in APs are uniform via Brun–Titchmarsh-type results, with p up to X^{1−ε}... For X = polylog(p) the uniformity fails — the coefficient 4p is huge relative to X. Hmm: the sieve dimension is 1, the sifting range is primes ≤ z; for values 4Cp+1 ≤ 4Xp, we sieve by primes up to z ≈ X^{1/2}: the count of C ≤ X with 4Cp+1 free of primes ≤ z is ≪ X/log z — that's fine and uniform in p (only the residue of p mod q matters). So #{C ≤ X: 4Cp+1 has no prime factor ≤ X^{1/2}} ≪ X/log X — pointwise in p! But 'rich' needs ≥ 6 factors, not just one small factor.) Refine: with k-fold sieving (Erdős–Kac-type for linear forms, Halberstam) one gets most C have ω(4Cp+1) ≈ log log(Xp)… uniformity in p needs the Turán–Kubilius inequality for linear forms with large coefficient — it holds! (The variance Σ_C (ω(4Cp+1) − log log)² ≪ X log log, uniformly in p, since it only uses residues of p mod small primes.)
why: A genuinely pointwise-in-p statement: for any fixed p and X ≥ (log p)^A, almost all C ≤ X have ω(4Cp+1) ≥ 6 (indeed ≈ log log Xp). So 'poor' failures are a vanishing fraction of C. Combined with the Kneser dichotomy, ES(p) would follow if 'periodic rich failures' could be shown not to happen for ALL C — a cleaner target (Galois-type: 'for some C, the prime factors of 4Cp+1 generate a subgroup containing −1 AND the subset-product set is not periodic-avoiding').
first_step: Prove the Turán–Kubilius bound for ω(4Cp+1), C ≤ X, uniform in p (standard; write it out with explicit constants); then count 'rich failures' empirically for p ≤ 10⁵ to see whether they are rare.
refs: Halberstam, 'On the distribution of additive number-theoretic functions' (1955)

repo_status.note: Turán–Kubilius/Erdős–Kac only generic or for shifts of p; no sieve over C for ω(4Cp+1).

title: Positive definite binary forms of discriminant −4(tp+1)… and the A/A* pairing as an ambiguous-form question
connection: Factorisations N = A·A* correspond to ambiguous forms/ideals of discriminant related to N. Words are factorisations with A ≡ A* ≡ −1 (mod t). Genus theory of disc −4N tells which ambiguous classes exist.
why: Gauss's genus theory counts factorisations as ambiguous classes, and the mod-t condition becomes a genus-character condition, a native class-group statement.
first_step: For small t, compute the genus characters of the ambiguous forms of disc −4N_t and identify which genus the word factorisations occupy.

repo_status.evidence: Gauss genus theory; ambiguous classes ⇔ factorisations of Δ

title: Explicit Burgess constants (Treviño-type) for the Legendre-sum T(p) in M_BM
connection: Helfgott needed fully explicit major arcs; the ES analogue is an explicit version of Thm 2.2 (M_BM(p) ≥ (3/16π² − o(1)) log²p), whose o(1) comes from Burgess on Σ(−m/p)w(m).
why: An explicit M_BM ≥ c·log²p for all p ≥ p₁ is a prerequisite of every H⁻_BM-type route and is purely a bookkeeping task with existing explicit Burgess inequalities.
first_step: Treviño, 'The Burgess inequality and the least kth power non-residue', IJNT 11 (2015) 1653–1678, arXiv:1412.3062 gives explicit Burgess estimates (verified, data/z52b/upgrades_leads_check.md); check that its ranges cover the weighted hyperbolic sum T(p) and compute the resulting explicit p₁.

title: Minimal counterexample via the e-slice: ES(p) from data of N = (p+e)/4 < p
connection: Four-colour and many combinatorial proofs consider a minimal counterexample. ES(p) ⟸ a property P(N, e) of the smaller integer N = (p+e)/4. Find a property Q(n), inherited along n ↦ (n + e)/4 for some e, such that Q(n) for all n < p implies Q(p) and Q(p) ⇒ ES(p).
why: A successful Q would make ES a consequence of verification (10¹⁸) + induction.
first_step: Data mining: for each p ≤ 10⁷, list e for which N_e carries a certificate and look for a hereditary property of N_e.

title: Ultraproduct transfer between F_q[T]-ES and ℤ-ES statements
connection: Ax–Kochen: first-order statements true for F_p((t)) for almost all p transfer to Q_p for almost all p. ES over F_q[T] has proved variants; ES is first-order over (ℤ, +, ·) (∀n ∃x,y,z), but Ax–Kochen transfers statements about valued fields (ℚ_p vs F_p((t))), not about ℤ with positivity; identify which ES-adjacent statements are about local/valued-field structures (and hence transferable) — reviewer repair.
why: Clarifies precisely which ES-type statements a model-theoretic transfer could ever reach (and that the full statement likely cannot).
first_step: Formulate ES sub-statements with bounded quantifier complexity (e.g. 'a certificate with C dividing a fixed polynomial in p') and check whether they are decidable/transferable.
areas: ES variants, function fields & other rings

repo_status.note: Ax-Kochen transfer classification of ES sub-statements not carried out.

title: Uniformity obstruction for linear-forms-in-primes certificate schemes at fixed p
connection: For fixed p, ES has finitely many solutions with denominators bounded polynomially in p (not O(p²): z can be ≍ p⁴, reviewer example x = (p+3)/4, y = (px+2)/3, z = pxy/2 for p ≡ 5 mod 24), and a fixed certificate parametrisation with auxiliary primes typically needs prime tuples of linear forms in a box polynomial in p with coefficients depending on p (many-to-one parametrisations need separate care). Green–Tao–Ziegler asymptotics are not uniform in coefficients comparable to the box, so they do not apply directly (correcting the BHS item).
why: Records precisely why the conditional→unconditional (Harpaz–Skorobogatov–Wittenberg) move does not transfer to ES as stated, and what uniformity would be needed.
first_step: State the needed uniform version: count of t ≤ T with L_i(t) all prime for forms with coefficients ≤ T^{1+ε}; compare with known uniform results (e.g. for a single form: Brun–Titchmarsh / Siegel–Walfisz ranges).
refs: arXiv:math/0404188 (Green-Tao, primes contain arbitrarily long APs)

title: No minor arcs: positivity lets ES discard all but the smallest levels
connection: Goldbach-type proofs must bound minor arcs because terms cancel. ES counts are sums of nonnegative level counts, R(p) = Σ_C D_C(p) ≥ Σ_{C ≤ K} D_C(p); so ES ⟸ a certificate among levels C ≤ K = (log p)^A, where the expected count is still ≍ (log p)·(log K) → ∞. The whole problem is a lower bound for a short, explicit 'major-level' sum.
why: Reframes which part of the analytic machinery is needed: only lower bounds on a few explicit structured counts, no cancellation estimates for the bulk.
first_step: For p in the hard lists, find the least K(p) such that some level ≤ K(p) carries a certificate, and fit K(p) against (log p)^A.

repo_status.note: Least major-level K(p) for certificates not fitted.
